title: How to Export Snowflake Logs
content_md: “Snowflake logs” means one of two things, and the export works the same for both. It can be security data your team stores in Snowflake tables. Or it can be Snowflake’s own audit trail, the SNOWFLAKE.ACCOUNT_USAGE views such as LOGIN_HISTORY and QUERY_HISTORY. For small pulls, run the query in SnowSQL with JSON output. For anything bigger, unload with COPY INTO a stage using FILE_FORMAT = (TYPE = JSON), and download the files with GET. Snowflake’s own logs drew a lot of attention in 2024, when attackers used stolen credentials to log in to customer accounts that didn’t enforce MFA. Login and query history are now standard asks in an investigation. Prime Core has more than 24,000 unique detection rules, mapped to 676 MITRE ATT&CK techniques. Below is how to get the data out, sanitize it, and investigate it for free in LogTotal. Before you start Access to ACCOUNT_USAGE . By default, only ACCOUNTADMIN can read these views. Other roles need the IMPORTED PRIVILEGES grant on the SNOWFLAKE database, or one of its database roles. Latency and retention. ACCOUNT_USAGE views keep a year of history but lag behind by up to a couple of hours. For the last seven days with no lag, the INFORMATION_SCHEMA.LOGIN_HISTORY table function is an alternative. A warehouse. Queries and unloads need a running warehouse, and they consume credits. Filter by time.
